categories.justification: The output explains mechanisms (MOVED redirects and topology refresh, node-timeout-bounded failover, async replication loss, why replicas do not protect against whole-cluster or logical failure) and quantifies where the case allows. It covers specific tradeoffs and edge cases such as retry amplification, false failovers and hot key ranges.
quotes: Replicas protect against losing a node, not against correlated or logical failure.
Aggressive client retries shorten the window in which users see errors, but they can amplify load on the surviving nodes during failover unless backoff and jitter are used
A legacy service, cron job or config still points at sess-redis-01.
